questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How top chefs create new recipes for restaurants
Why sugar is so bad for our teeth
The link between what we eat and how we feel
How to lose weight quickly before summer
questions.why: Sam says they'll be investigating the connection between our food and our mood.

questions.q: What does Rob say about most comfort food?
options: It's full of carbs and sugar, so we soon feel worse
It is healthy as long as you eat it slowly
It makes us feel better for many hours afterwards
It is mostly eaten by children and teenagers
questions.why: He says it's high in carbohydrates and sugar and after a few minutes leaves us feeling worse.

questions.q: What happens to chef Danny Edwards' appetite when he works in a busy kitchen?
options: It gets much bigger
It stays the same
He only wants sweet food
It often goes down
questions.why: He says your appetite can become suppressed and you sometimes don't want to eat.

questions.q: Why do many chefs have quite a bad diet, according to Danny?
options: They don't really like eating their own cooking
They grab something quick on the go
They only eat once a day, late at night
Restaurant food is too expensive for them
questions.why: He says it's often grabbing something on the go, something quick.

questions.q: What did Professor Felice Jacka find in her study?
options: Those who got better had also eaten better
Medicine worked much better than a healthy diet
Diet had no real effect on depression at all
Only olive oil and fish helped the patients
questions.why: She found the patients whose mental health improved were those who had improved their diet.

questions.q: How did other doctors react to Professor Jacka's idea at first?
options: They were very excited and wanted to help
They offered to help her with the study
They were sceptical and sometimes patronising
They ignored it completely for many years
questions.why: She says they were 'hugely sceptical and sometimes very patronising'.

questions.q: Why does Professor Jacka think doctors reacted like that?
options: Because her study was badly designed and small
Because she was too young and had no experience
Because food companies were paying them
Because they get almost no nutrition training
questions.why: She says doctors and psychiatrists get almost no nutrition training during their studies.

questions.q: What does Rob suggest doing when you feel down?
options: Eat a donut to give yourself energy
Eat an apple instead of a donut
Skip your next meal and drink water
Visit a restaurant with some friends
questions.why: He says when your brain wants a donut, you might be better eating an apple.
